task.description: Implement the validated design at lib/letflow/design/iss-0047-username-race-conflict-target.md (design gate PASSed, see handoffs/WF03-ISS0047-20260818/step-02b-code-design-validator.json). Fixes ISS-0047 in lib/letflow/identity.ex's insert_or_fetch/4: replace the {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} passthrough with the three-way branch specified in the design (username_unique_conflict?/1, get_by_username/2, identity_matches?/2 helpers), falling through to the existing unmodified re_select_on_conflict/3 when the losing racer's identity matches, otherwise propagating the original error unchanged. Follow the design doc's exact function/line-level specification -- do not deviate from its logic shape without flagging why. Implement in lib/ only; do NOT write the new :auto-mode regression test yourself (that's TEST-DESIGNER's job at Step 4) -- but you may sanity-check your own implementation against a throwaway scratch script if useful, per core-directives.md's No Speculation rule, then delete the scratch script.
acceptance_criteria: insert_or_fetch/4 implements the three-way branch exactly as designed: identical-identity race resolves via re_select_on_conflict/3; genuine unrelated username collision still propagates {:error, changeset}.

New helpers (username_unique_conflict?/1, get_by_username/2, identity_matches?/2 or equivalently named per the design) added with @spec, matching the module's existing typespec/documentation conventions.

Existing test/letflow/identity_test.exs suite (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/identity_test.exs) passes unchanged -- especially the genuine-collision test at lines 379-394 and the existing REQ-018 race test.
No changes to upsert_by_external_identity/4's or re_select_on_conflict/3's existing logic (design specifies they stay untouched).

result.summary: Implemented the design's three-way branch in insert_or_fetch/4 (lib/letflow/identity.ex): replaced the bare {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} = error -> error clause with a branch that calls the new username_unique_conflict?/1 to detect a username-uniqueness changeset error, then get_by_username/2 + identity_matches?/2 to distinguish the racing-opponent case (falls through to the unmodified re_select_on_conflict/3) from a genuine unrelated collision (propagates {:error, changeset} unchanged). All three new helpers added as private functions with @spec, placed alongside get_by_external_identity/3, matching the module's existing conventions. upsert_by_external_identity/4, the on_conflict Repo.insert/2 call, its {:ok, ...} branch, and re_select_on_conflict/3 are byte-for-byte unchanged, matching design section 4's do-not-change list. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` passes cleanly. `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/identity_test.exs` cannot run: the test FILE fails to compile with a pre-existing SystemLimitError (a describe/test name at line 379 exceeds ExUnit's 255-character test-name limit) -- confirmed via `git stash` that this same failure occurs identically on the pre-change code, so it is NOT a regression introduced by this change, but it does mean the acceptance criterion 'existing suite passes unchanged' cannot be positively verified in this environment right now. Flagging to TEST-RUNNER/ORCH as a pre-existing, unrelated blocker (introduced by an earlier commit that added identity_test.exs's REQ-063 username-collision describe/test block, not by ISS-0047's fix) that needs a test-file edit (shortening the describe/test name) before this suite -- or any future work touching identity.ex -- can be verified by compiling/running the file at all.

issues.description: test/letflow/identity_test.exs fails to compile under ExUnit 1.18.3 (Elixir 1.18.3 / OTP 27) with SystemLimitError: computed test name at line 379 ('test provision_oidc_user/4 — username collision, same tenant schema vs different tenant schemas (REQ-063 acceptance criteria) two users with the same username in the SAME tenant schema: the second JIT provisioning call fails with a username uniqueness changeset error') exceeds ExUnit's 255-character limit. Reproduced identically before this change via `git stash`. Not caused by ISS-0047's fix; pre-exists in the test file since at least the REQ-063 commit. Needs a test-file change (shorten the describe block name and/or the test name) -- out of scope for ELIXIR-DEV per this task's 'do not touch test files' instruction.
